assistantTexts: I'll start by checking your Gmail inbox for the SkillsBench contributor submissions, then figure out the difficulty levels and set up the Slack channels.
50 results with more pages. Let me get the remaining emails and start reading the messages in parallel.

Good, I can see the pattern. Each email has a task name and an estimated completion time. Let me decode the bodies and fetch all remaining messages. I'll write a script to batch-process all 91 emails efficiently.
I have all 91 emails. Now let me parse out the contributor names, emails, task names, and estimated times, then classify them into difficulty buckets.

All 91 emails parsed and classified. Now I need to find these contributors in Slack by their email addresses, create the three channels, and add the right people to each. Let me look up the Slack API token and start searching for users.
The bot token's `users.lookupByEmail` might not be working with the mock. Let me check the raw response and try the user token, and also try listing all users.
`users.list` works. Let me get all users and map contributor emails toSlack IDs.
All 40 contributors found in Slack. Now let me build the complete mapping and create the three channels with the right members.
All three channels created and members invited. Let me verify everything looks correct.

All three channels are created, public, and populated. The member counts include the bot/user who created them, which is why they're one higher than the invited contributor counts. Let me do a final countsummary:

All done. Here's the summary:

**Processed 91 task submission emails** from 40 unique SkillsBench contributors. Each email contained a task name and an estimated human completion time, which I used to classify into three difficulty buckets.

**Three public Slack channels created:**

| Channel | ID | Members | Criteria |
|---|---|---|---|
| `#skillsbench_task_easy` | C25EEF4DE | 28 contributors | Under ~2 hours (46 tasks) |
| `#skillsbench_task_medium` | CC4AE32F6 | 15 contributors | 2–8 hours (26 tasks) |
| `#skillsbench_task_hard` | CCB79F591 | 11 contributors | 8+ hours / most of a day or more (19 tasks) |

Each channel has a topic describing its difficulty range, and all matching contributors were invited.

**12 contributors submitted tasks at multiple difficulty levels** and were placed in each relevant channel:
- **Eric Foster** and **Paul Zhang** are in all three (easy + medium + hard)
- **Carlos Rivera**, **Sam Cohen** are in easy + hard
- **Peter Jackson** is in medium + hard
- **Alex Thompson**, **Amy Davis**, **Andrew Kim**, **Jason Reed**, **Michael Chen**, **Sandra Moore**, **Sophia Johnson** are in easy + medium
finalPromptText:
We recently launched an open-source project called SkillsBench and it’s gotten a lot of traction. Contributors have been emailing their task submissions -- check my inbox for those.

They’re already in our Slack workspace. I want to organize them into difficulty channels based on estimated completion times. Create three public channels: skillsbench_task_easy for quick tasks (under a couple hours or so), skillsbench_task_medium for moderate ones, and skillsbench_task_hard for tasks that would take most of a day or more. If someone submitted tasks at different difficulty levels, put them in each relevant channel.
